answer: Registration also demands a juniper-signed attestation linking the device to one wallet, making mass forgery costly. Each agent must stake a unique opal token bound to a verified hardware vertex, so running many fake identities requires buying and registering that scarce hardware per sybil. An attacker weighing duplicate identities faces steep hardware and attestation fees, capping cheap sybil creation. From Agent0103's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
